active_assets.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: outdoor background panorama for a side-view hamster platform game. Attached hamster is the style reference.
White paper, BLACK INK only. Sparse raw pen sketch with bold imperfect outer strokes and a few finer botanical lines. A LITTLE believable anatomy in tree trunks and branches, but very minimalist. No gray fills or shading.
A quiet open meadow at the edge of a woodland: two loosely drawn slender deciduous trees off-center, natural branching trunks and a few leaf clusters, low distant rolling hills, one sparse clump of tall grass near an edge. The whole upper half is wide empty white SKY. Lots of open breathing room in the middle for the hamster. No roof, masonry, arches, cave, dungeon, buildings or enclosed spaces.
Wide 3:1 panorama, flat side elevation. Distant trees stand on the same soft distant horizon around the lower quarter; the very bottom stays empty white. Keep foreground gameplay separate: NO foreground floor, platforms, floating logs, fences or gates. Tree masses must be airy line drawings, not dense black or gray filled canopies. Selected thick black trunk edges, a few branch forks, economical natural shapes; no repeated cartoon bubble canopy, no realistic rendering, gradients, shadows, detailed bark texture, full foliage, dense hatching or decoration.
No characters, text, labels, borders or UI. The feeling is an outdoor white-paper indie comic, understated and a little rough, with believable natural forms.

palette: White object fills and sky; black ink lines. No gray washes, colored surfaces, gradients, or dark atmosphere.
setting: One continuous outdoor route: three 4000-pixel sections, the 6000-pixel Contrary Crossing, then the 7940-pixel Honking Meadow. All five retain three log piles. Level four combines logs with two linked-switch rope bridges, a cover ambush and a runaway flag whose switch is at the far end beyond its snare. Level five introduces bell-triggered charging geese, breakable fences and a final bell with a spare Echo for the predator bush. Floating collectibles are disabled everywhere. Flags are checkpoints. Old sections retire only after leaving the view, and lock out backtracking.

font.delivery: Locally embedded Roman and Italic faces in src/theme-type.css

unused_asset_specs.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: transparent outdoor terrain sheet for a white-paper 2D hamster platform game, TWO equal horizontal rows on 1536x1024.
Style reference: attached hamster. WHITE solid object interiors, BLACK sketch ink contours. Slightly believable natural forms but very economical: heavy uneven outer strokes, few finer inner lines, sparse raw pen drawing. No color, gray shading, gradients, shadows or background.
TOP ROW y0-511: ONE continuous side-on EARTH BANK strip spanning the full image width. A flat walkable top edge at y125, with nothing projecting above it. Beneath: an irregular white soil cut face descending to y500, a few embedded stones of unequal sizes and two small exposed roots; no masonry courses or repeated brick pattern. Thick black uneven top edge, a few short thin soil lines only. Left/right same height to tile; open white soil face, no solid black underground fill. Transparent ABOVE the bank, bank itself solid white.
BOTTOM ROW y512-1023: ONE horizontal fallen TREE LOG from x70..1466, flat usable top y640, bottom y820. Slightly irregular outline, blunt cut end on the left with two loose growth rings, one small knot, just two short lengthwise wood grain lines. No leaves, grass, supports, branches or dangling objects; the game draws the supporting stumps separately so they root in the real terrain. Transparent around the log. Simple hand-drawn wooden beam, not stone.
Keep every piece fully within its row, no overlap across y512. No text, labels, grid, backdrop, other objects or UI. The whole sheet should feel like spare black-pen natural scenery drawn for the exact hamster reference.

terrain.style: Continuous raised grass banks, white fills, black outlines, sparse grass and tiny dirt marks; no exposed roots or supports. World-anchored sample vertices prevent slope twitching when the camera moves. The short downhill grade is 90 pixels long, replacing the abrupt 20-pixel descent. Gentle grades stay walkable; genuinely steep descents use gravity. Feet cannot pass through solid soil; real gaps remain open.
terrain.sections: The first three sections have three Echo puzzles each. Level one never fires aimed attacks. The first puzzles in levels two and three always attack when their authored escape remains valid. Level two uses terrain cover; level three requires jumping its 150-pixel collapsing retreat hole onto solid ground. Their last puzzles retain random attacks with cover; flat middle switches remain harmless. Level four has linked rope bridges and a runaway flag. Grounded direction changes brake immediately for a quick retreat.

log_piles.behavior: Large tightly packed 24-log stacks, taller than a normal jump. Plate press flings randomized spinning debris with gravity, ground bounces and flat settling. On release, debris fades out sequentially as new pieces pop into place locally, bottom to top, in 0.72 seconds. Rebuild entry only records whether the hamster was caught; it never deals invisible damage. Crushing waits until a visible newly built piece intersects that hamster. Empty upper corners are safe, and leaving the pile clears eligibility. Later entrants are blocked or pushed out without a new crushing check. Collision follows each visible piece's rounded shape, rotation, scale and pop position. Flying and rebuilding animations keep advancing during death, then all piles reset and flying pieces clear when the hamster respawns.
log_piles.damage: Ordinary scatter is harmless. Level one never fires aimed attacks. The opening puzzles in levels two and three guarantee attacks with valid escape terrain; last puzzles retain 50% / 70% chances. Fresh player or Echo presses can trigger attacks aimed at the presser. Joining a held plate never rearms it. Once a killer attack is triggered, its windup and launch finish even after the plate is released, an Echo vanishes, or the player dies. Re-pressing cannot duplicate an active hostile volley from that pile. Once launched, all logs finish their flight even after release. All 24 standard hostile logs lift over 0.22 seconds, launch at 0.46 seconds, and continue in their captured direction at constant velocity until their whole body exits the camera. Hits do not delete projectiles. Terrain or roof impacts deflect them into harmless ballistic debris. Capsule collision checks cover before the hamster's 34x61 body.

sky_message.placement: World-anchored above the first death location; bold IM Fell English, no overlay. Once it leaves either camera edge, it disappears immediately and is permanently dismissed in saved memory. Later deaths never create another message. Restart all levels begins a fresh run.

echo.behavior: Two Echoes replay independently. Each replays the complete last three seconds, or all actions so far for a younger recording, at normal speed. Switch contact never trims the approach or teleports the clone to the current player. Recorded waits remain part of the replay. E is black when a slot is free and white when both are occupied; two small ink slots above it show capacity. Q vanishes both clones and starts a fresh clip while retaining the previous recording for immediate reuse. Fresh footsteps replace that fallback when enough have been recorded. Death and section changes clear both recordings. Respawn resets the world to its initial puzzle positions. Each clone has a separate circle timer with I or II ticks. Overlapping clones are slightly separated visually without moving their real switch contacts; offscreen clones retain a small edge timer and direction mark. No dotted playback paths or numeric countdowns.

sprite_rendering: Main-pose alpha bounds exclude detached pixels from the preceding row in run frames four/five and jump frame five. Original sheet and equal frame assets remain unchanged.
linked_bridges: Level four has two 460-pixel gaps. Each rope bridge needs its own pair of marked switches held simultaneously. The second pair also controls a log pile that blocks access to the other switch, combining the old and new mechanics. Hinged wooden halves unfold over 0.6 seconds and become walkable only when level; release folds them back over 0.4 seconds. Both banks meet the deck at the same height. Ropes connect the deck rails to posts anchored on the creek banks. No floating supports.
homing_shed: The first log puzzle in level four flings all 24 logs upward and sideways out of the camera. Each waits invisibly for three seconds after exiting. All 24 logs return after their delay once triggered; releasing the switch or vanishing an Echo cannot cancel them, even before the first return launches. They return from above the current camera and home toward the hamster within the encounter area. A second press cannot create a duplicate volley while those logs are active. A 150-pixel-wide open shed stands after the switch on a long, uninterrupted flat grass bank. The switch, forward shelter, log pile, and second bridge switch follow in that order. Two substantial 12-pixel wooden posts sit level on the ground beneath a simple pitched plank roof. Every roof impact bounces the log upward and sideways as harmless spinning debris under gravity. An Echo can keep the switch held while the hamster runs forward into shelter. Longer final-pose holds in level four allow time for the return volley and the linked crossing.
drawing_order: Packed piles draw top rows first and bottom rows last, so the bottom row is in front. Projectiles draw only their log shapes, without speed lines or arrow trails. Pressure plates draw above all logs and projectiles to remain visible.
runaway_flag: After both bridge puzzles, approaching within 220 pixels makes the final flag sprout running legs and flee at 390 pixels per second. It patrols only solid ground and cannot be completed by merely passing the section boundary. The five-stroke switch sits at the far end, 20 pixels before the section boundary and beyond the rope snare. Follow the flag all the way there, leave an Echo on that switch, then head back to the snare. An Echo on the switch holds the rope snare; the flag is caught when it crosses the snare. Catching up to the trapped flag completes the fourth level. Retry resets the flag and bridges.
ambient_animation: Always enabled automatically. Six idle poses, gently swaying grass and distant trees, moving creek ripples and fluttering flags. No floating collectibles. Menu contains Resume, Restart, Sound and trail selection.
death_animation: Backward ballistic knockback with a tumbling body, flicker after 0.38 seconds, disappearance at 0.9 seconds. Camera eases back to the section spawn. World animations continue through the death sequence. At respawn the world resets fully: sliding cover returns home and can trigger again; log piles are restored; flying logs and pending attacks are cleared; geese, fences, bushes, bridges, flags and collapse holes return to their initial states. Echoes and old clips remain cleared. Trail progress, learned memory and the first-death message history persist.

goose_trail.style: White paper with spare black marker outlines. A simple long-necked white goose has animated feet, a flapping wing, an angry warning pose, and a harmless dazed return. Wooden bell posts and tall breakable picket fences stand directly on the ground.
goose_trail.behavior: Every fresh bell press rearms its goose, even during a warning, chase or return. Contacts joining a continuously held plate never ring again. The first and last geese capture the presser position and charge straight at 740 / 920 pixels per second after 0.75 / 0.55 seconds. The second gives a 0.35-second warning, rushes into view at 684 pixels per second while over 200 pixels away, then matches the hamster at 285 pixels per second nearby, leaving enough clearance for a timely jump. It tracks the hamster until physically crashing into raised ground; passing its original target never ends the chase. Real body, neck, head and beak collisions deal damage. Charges break fences; impacts stun the goose before its harmless walk home. Fresh presses can interrupt any phase. Death does not freeze animation; explicit retry resets the encounter.
goose_trail.puzzles: Encounter bases are 0, 2720 and 5610. Three bell plates each scatter their own log pile. The second grassy rise slides left at the hamster running speed (285 pixels per second) for three seconds after its first bell ring, remaining continuous ground with sloped sides and no legs or block seams. Its full travel stays on a flat solid bank; grounded riders move with it. It cannot retrigger until explicit retry. The final puzzle uses one bell plate, leaving a spare Echo to watch the bush. Three-second recordings hold their final pose for twenty-two seconds in this longer trail. The player must cross two creeks, all three fences and all three log piles. The predator always starts 1250 pixels before the third bell, before the final creek, leaving room to establish a watcher before the goose puzzle.

predator_bush.introduction: Harmless berry bushes establish the safe silhouette throughout earlier trails. The sole berryless predator always starts at local x=5010, 1250 pixels before the third bell, on the bank before the final creek. This leaves an approach and a creek crossing between the bush encounter and the last goose. Every respawn restores the same placement.
predator_bush.style: Use the user-supplied bush artwork directly. Every stationary bush uses the first sprite of the first row. Harmless plants add three or four spaced individual ink berries, with subtle seeded size and mirror variation. The killer has no berries. No generated replacement outline, generated teeth, idle row cycling, extra leaf strokes or added facial details.
predator_bush.behavior: The berryless plant remains dormant and harmless until the hamster passes more than 60 pixels beyond it. Once activated, it pursues at 315 pixels per second only while neither the hamster nor an active Echo faces it within 720 pixels. It jumps over reachable obstacles, follows airborne players, and jumps creek gaps to pursue into the last encounter. Gravity and solid surfaces still apply while watched or biting; it cannot walk through cliffs or piles. Echo facing, expiry and Q affect watching immediately. Respawn and explicit retry both disarm the plant and restore its home position before the third bell.
predator_bush.attack: Within 78 horizontal pixels and the actual mouth height, proximity starts a 0.22-second enlargement and gaping black mouth with two rows of sharp white teeth. Watching cannot make close contact safe. A quick high jump or moving out of reach cancels the bite. If the hamster remains in range, it is pulled toward the mouth and shrinks away over 0.38 seconds, while the bush keeps chomping during the death sequence. This replaces knockback only for a bush death. The standard checkpoint camera return, cleared Echoes, and first-death sky message still apply. After chewing, the plant returns to its ordinary berryless silhouette. Retry restores its starting position.
predator_bush.solution: After crossing the second log pile, leave an Echo facing the berryless plant, jump past it, then cross the creek before using the second Echo at the third bell. The encounters are separated by 1250 pixels rather than overlapping on the final rise.

sprite_sheet.grid: 7 columns x 2 rows; each padded cell 512x384; shared anchor (256,360)
rows: top row: seven user-drawn moving frames; first frame is the default for all bushes
bottom row: seven user-drawn eating frames; huge gape, gulp and closing poses preserved
sprite_sheet.preparation: The supplied 2048x576 file has seven distinct drawings in each logical row, with a large bite extending into neighboring nominal cells. The generator decodes the RGBA PNG, isolates the fourteen connected drawings, retains their original pixels and antialiased edges, and aligns their base contact lines in roomy cells. Source file remains unchanged. No scaling, recoloring or synthesized poses in the asset.
sprite_sheet.integration: Movement advances through the supplied top row by traveled distance. Idle, dormant and watched bushes use the first top-row drawing. Opening selects the first five attack poses, swallowing holds the huge gape, then plays the supplied gulp and closing drawings. The attack faces the nearby hamster. A clipped redraw of the same supplied mouth pixels forms the foreground during swallowing; no generated teeth are added.

hollow_tree.reference: User's November 4 sketch: tall open trunk, alternating inward rectangular ledges, one large sweeping right branch with a sparse irregular outline.
hollow_tree.renderer: src/art.js tree and woodPlatform; existing canvas ink drawing system
hollow_tree.behavior: The sixth trail contains only the tree and thirteen safe ledges spaced 100 pixels vertically. Camera follows the full climb. No switches, enemies, extra puzzles or finish flag. Work in progress appears above the top; reaching it does not show a completed-game dialog.

help: The question-mark dialog contains controls only, followed by collapsed, numbered Hint 1 / Hint 2 / Hint 3 entries for new mechanics in the current trail. Hints follow introduction order: Echo plates; aimed logs; collapsing retreat; linked bridges, homing logs with shed, runaway flag; bells with geese, sliding grassy cover, predator bush. The unfinished sixth trail only describes climbing the tree. No future-level mechanics or automatic full walkthrough.
